title: Sonay Kartal's Comeback Rolls On to the Wuhan Open Semifinals
summary:
British tennis player Sonay Kartal is on a remarkable comeback. The 24-year-old beat fifth seed Elina Svitolina of Ukraine 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 in the quarterfinals of the Wuhan Open in China.

Kartal missed more than six months of tennis with a stress fracture in her back. Because of that long break, her world ranking dropped to 170, even though she had reached a career-high ranking of 44 last summer. She is using a protected ranking, a rule that helps injured players enter tournaments, to play in Wuhan. The win over Svitolina was her sixth victory in eight matches since returning.

Kartal has been beating strong players all week. In earlier rounds, she defeated Italian 15th seed Jasmine Paolini and Swiss ninth seed Belinda Bencic. She had not lost a single set on her way to the quarterfinals.

Against Svitolina, Kartal broke her opponent's serve early to take the first set. Svitolina, who is ranked sixth in the world, took a medical timeout for treatment on her right arm, then came back strongly to win the second set. The third set was close until Kartal broke Svitolina's serve at 5-4 to win the match.

"It was solid composure from me throughout," Kartal said. "It's breaking new ground for me this week." She also thanked the crowd for the amazing atmosphere.

Kartal is only the second British player, after Johanna Konta, to reach a semifinal at this top level of tournament, called WTA 1000, since it began in 2009. On Saturday, she will face Jeļena Ostapenko, who won the French Open in 2017.
why_it_matters: Kartal's run shows how an athlete can return from a serious injury and compete with the world's best, putting her among very few British players to reach this stage.
